WHY THE STARSHIP CATCH MATTERS
Catching the Super Heavy booster with the tower arms isn’t just a cool stunt — it’s the key that unlocks true rapid reusability.

Here’s why it’s so important:

• Speed of reuse
Landing in the ocean or on a droneship still requires recovery ships, transport back to the pad, and significant refurbishment. Catching the booster directly at the launch tower means it can potentially be restacked and flown again in hours or days instead of weeks.
• Cost
The rocket is the most expensive part of spaceflight. If you can catch and reuse the booster with minimal work, the cost per kilogram to orbit drops dramatically. This is the path to Starship’s target of under $100/kg.
• Flight cadence
A multiplanetary civilization and large-scale orbital industry require flying often. High cadence only becomes realistic when both the booster and ship can be turned around quickly. The tower catch is what makes that possible for the first stage.
• Closing the loop
Falcon 9 proved reuse works. Starship aims for both stages to be fully and rapidly reusable. Catching the booster is the biggest remaining milestone for the first stage.
Everything else — Mars missions, lunar bases, orbital data centers, heavy cargo — becomes far more practical once you can catch the booster and fly it again quickly.

BREAKING: Tesla will open source the design and software of the Model S and Model X. 🚗⚡

• Elon Musk says Tesla plans to release the complete design and software for both vehicles.
• The move follows Tesla's 2023 open-source release of the original Roadster's engineering and diagnostic materials.
• Production of the Model S and Model X ended in Q2 2026, with factory capacity redirected to Optimus and Cybercab.
• Open-sourcing the platforms will make repairs, maintenance, and modifications easier for owners and independent repair shops.
• Engineers and researchers will gain access to real-world EV battery, powertrain, and software designs.

The decision continues Tesla's long-standing commitment to open innovation and supporting the broader transition to sustainable transportation.

ELON Musk SHUTS DOWN THE “DOGE KILLED PEOPLE” CLAIM

In the Economist interview, the editor pushed the idea that DOGE cuts to USAID caused deaths.

Elon’s response was blunt:
“Zero.”
When pressed, he called the claims “false… nonsense and absolute nonsense.”
He explained that legitimate programs were moved to the State Department, and that when you cut funding to fraudulent or ineffective organizations, the people who lost the money never admit it was waste. They invent the most sympathetic story possible to get the funding restored.
That’s exactly what happened.
The media ran with the emotional narrative. Elon stuck to the facts.
